subject: Mutual action plan: multiphase pool placement & staged burst policy
messages:
From: Alexa Torres <alexa.torres@auroracorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: devops-leads@auroracorp.com, procurement@auroracorp.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool activation - placement questions

Hi Soojin / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to get the plan for the Dedicated GPU pool scoped so our procurement and NetOps teams can greenlight the AP/EP approvals. Attached is a quick ramp profile with expected token throughput per environment and a short note on compliance windows (business hours + EU night batch jobs).

High-level asks from our side:
- Preferred region for primary serving (we currently route EU traffic to eu-west1).
- Whether you can provide a staged burst policy (e.g., +25% baseline for month 1, +50% month 2) tied to autoscale thresholds.
- What telemetry we should expect in the first 72 hours (per-route latency and token cost breakdown).

We'd like to propose a tight kickoff next Tuesday (6/30) for the mutual action plan and a go/no-go checkpoint two weeks after. Please advise on required lead times if additional GPUs or a burst buffer are needed.

Attachments: Aurora-Ramp-Profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Alexa Torres
Head of ML Ops, Aurora Corp
alexa.torres@auroracorp.com
+44 20 5555 1212

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Torres <alexa.torres@auroracorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: multiphase pool placement & staged burst policy

Alexa — great to get this. Appreciate the ramp profile, that helps a lot. I pulled the team together and sketched a mutual action plan below so we can align prerequisites and owners before kickoff. I've attached a short multipool template for your NetOps folks to review (RI-multipool-template.yaml).

Proposed mutual action plan (owners + due dates):
1) Confirm primary/fallback regions (Aurora): due 6/24 — owner: Aurora NetOps.
   - Our recommendation: eu-west1 primary, us-central as warm fallback for failover.
2) Baseline capacity sizing and burst buffer request: due 6/25 — owner: Redwood (Rishi + Soojin).
   - Please confirm baseline QPS and concurrent session estimates from the ramp profile.
3) Autoscale policy draft & thresholds: due 6/27 — owner: Redwood (Rishi).
   - Suggested approach: two-tier autoscale: baseline autoscale (0-85% utilization) + staged burst buffer triggered at 85-92%, with temporary burst up to +60% for controlled windows.
4) Security/compliance checklist and evidence exchange: due 6/28 — owner: Aurora sec + Redwood sec.
5) Kickoff & canary plan: scheduled 6/30 — joint. Go/no-go checkpoint 7/14.

Questions for Aurora (short):
- Can you confirm the expected concurrency at 95th pct during peak batch windows?
- Any data residency or network egress limits beyond eu-west1?
- Will you require an on-prem connector (we can run Private control plane) or is VPC acceptable?

Notes on telemetry: we will enable per-route latency, token-level cost breakdown, and a short-lived prefix K/V cache for the canary. We'll also surface incremental token cost within the Console during the first 72 hours.

Attachments: RI-multipool-template.yaml (text)

Looping in Rishi to scope the exact GPU SKUs and burst guardrails — Rishi, can you confirm if the requested +60% temporary burst needs reserved spare capacity or can be handled by a soft-burst from shared pools?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Alexa Torres <alexa.torres@auroracorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, devops-leads@auroracorp.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: multiphase pool placement & staged burst policy

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful. Quick answers:
- 95th pct concurrency during peak batch windows: ~420 concurrent sessions (we'll attach a breakdown to the ramp sheet).
- Data residency: EU-only for live traffic; batch jobs may originate from our US analytics cluster but results are EU-stored.
- On-prem connector: not required for now; VPC peering is fine.

A procurement question: if we rely on soft-burst from shared pools for the +60% temporary window, are there SLA protections if shared pool capacity is constrained? Specifically, we need clarity on failover time and whether SLA credits are available for burst shortfalls — procurement wants this in the SOW.

I also attached our security annex for the checklist (Aurora-Security-Annex.pdf).

Attachments: Aurora-Security-Annex.pdf (PDF)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Torres <alexa.torres@auroracorp.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, procurement@auroracorp.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: multiphase pool placement & staged burst policy

Hi Alexa — quick confirmation from ops and an updated asklist below so procurement can finish SOW language.

Operational decisions we will commit to:
- Primary region: eu-west1 (confirmed). Warm fallback: us-central with cross-region KV invalidation for session routing.
- Burst guardrails: baseline autoscale to 85% utilization; soft-burst allowed up to +40% without reserved capacity (best-effort).
- Controlled temporary burst (up to +60%) will require a 72-hour advance notice and a short reserved buffer (we'll reserve a small spare pool for the first two planned high-volume windows).
- Observability: 1s per-route latency metrics, per-token cost breakdown, and 5-minute histogram exports to your Splunk endpoint (we'll include the ingestion token exchange).

Procurement language suggestion (SOW excerpt):
"Redwood will provide baseline dedicated pool capacity as scoped in the mutual action plan. Soft-burst from Redwood shared capacity is best-effort and subject to availability; controlled bursts up to 60% require a 72-hour notification and a limited reserved buffer. SLA credits for unavailability during scheduled controlled bursts will be negotiated and documented in the final SOW."

Next steps:
- Aurora to confirm concurrency spreadsheet (due EOD 6/26).
- Redwood to share exact GPU SKU list and pricing addendum (Rishi) by 6/26.
- Joint kickoff 6/30 — calendar invite shortly.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
